subject.title: Generalize post-timeout compaction completion reconciliation across session state

question: Should OpenClaw promote the existing count-only late-success repair into an authoritative compaction-completion reconciliation boundary, and which session fields should that boundary own?
rationale: Source inspection shows the remaining design gap, but deciding whether the boundary owns only durable accounting or also status snapshots, outcome metadata, auth-profile rotation, memory flush state, plugin context-engine notifications, and recovery events is an architecture/product choice.

options.title: Design the boundary first
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical design item and have session-state owners define field ownership plus monotonic/idempotent semantics before implementation.

options.title: Keep narrow follow-ups
options.body: Continue using the count-only repair and handle stale status, activity, plugin-context, and recovery fields through separate focused issues or PRs without a shared completion boundary.

options.title: Declare current behavior sufficient
options.body: Close the broad follow-up if maintainers intentionally want only the shipped count reconciliation and no shared compaction-completion contract.

recommendation.title: Design the boundary first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical design item and have session-state owners define field ownership plus monotonic/idempotent semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the clearest recent history on the merged compaction reconciliation precursor and nearby session write seams likely to host this boundary.
